entries.effect: a destination: which page, which point on it and which zoom.  -initWithPage:atPoint: is the header's own designated initializer (PDFDestination.h:22) and is implemented because a class a program cannot construct answers a crash where the host answers an object - measured, and the measurement is in the harness's own init.* keys.  -init is implemented even though PDFDestination.h declares none, because the iOS 16.0 arm64e cache gives this class an own -init (own -init: 1) read with the tree's own census over that cache.  -initWithPage:atPoint: answers NO OBJECT for a nil page - measured, and found by the harness rather than asked for - so plain -init, which the host answers with an object, sets the members itself.  The NSCopying conformance is implemented: the copy is a new object whose PAGE IS THE SAME one, measured - a destination names a page and does not own it - with a zoom that is its own, and a destination with no page copies to an object too, which is why -copyWithZone: is not built through -initWithPage:atPoint:.  A destination read out of a document comes from the /D array of PDF 1.7 Table 8.42, [pageRef /XYZ left top zoom], and the page is resolved by IDENTITY of the page dictionary: this SDK has no object-number accessor, so CGPDFArrayGetDictionary follows the reference and the result is matched against CGPDFPageGetDictionary over the document's pages.
